phenomena.name: School Fragmentation
phenomena.description: The fish school splits into multiple spatially separated clusters during or after a shark encounter. This can be quantified by tracking the number of connected components or clusters (e.g., using a distance threshold) over time; fragmentation is indicated by an increase in the number of clusters and a decrease in the size of the largest cluster.

phenomena.name: School Elongation
phenomena.description: The overall shape of the fish school becomes elongated (stretched) in the direction of escape when threatened. Measured by the aspect ratio of the spatial covariance ellipse of fish positions; elongation corresponds to a higher ratio of the major to minor axis, often aligned with the average escape direction.

phenomena.name: Coordinated Escape Wave
phenomena.description: A collective directional movement away from the shark propagates through the school, characterized by a transient increase in the average alignment (polarization) and a spatial wave of direction changes emanating from the shark's location. This can be observed as a spatiotemporal pattern of high directional correlation and a moving front of aligned velocities.

phenomena.name: Fright Contagion Wave
phenomena.description: The frightened state spreads through the school as a wave, with a spatial gradient of frightened individuals moving outward from the initially frightened fish. Measured by the spatiotemporal distribution of the binary fright state; a wave is indicated by a expanding region of high fright probability and a time-lagged cross-correlation between fright states at different distances.

phenomena.name: Threat-Induced Polarization
phenomena.description: The school's global polarization (average alignment of fish orientations) increases in response to shark presence, as fish align their escape directions. Measured by the mean resultant length of heading vectors; a significant rise in polarization during threat periods compared to baseline indicates this phenomenon.

phenomena.name: Local Compaction
phenomena.description: Fish form denser local clusters (higher local density) in certain regions as a defensive response, possibly away from the shark or in areas of high fright. Measured by the average number of neighbors within a small radius or by kernel density estimates; compaction is seen as an increase in local density peaks and a decrease in nearest-neighbor distances.

phenomena.name: Vortex/Milling Formation
phenomena.description: The school exhibits rotational motion around a common center (milling), often as a response to conflicting social and threat forces. Measured by the curl of the velocity field or by the angular momentum of fish around the group centroid; a sustained nonzero average angular velocity indicates milling.

phenomena.name: Leader-Follower Directional Cascades
phenomena.description: A few individuals (leaders) initiate direction changes that propagate to others, leading to cascading alignment across the school. Measured by time-lagged cross-correlations of heading changes between pairs of fish and by the identification of influential individuals whose direction changes precede similar changes in neighbors.

Asymmetric turn requests around a component centroid can generate tangential motion and a nonzero cross product of component-relative position and velocity, increasing component mean angular momentum.

Turn requests that propagate from fish to neighbors can make current heading changes resemble previous-step neighbor heading changes; this dynamic propagation raises component mean lagged heading-change alignment.
